title: Individual Unemployability in the Opening Past-Due Release of Disability Compensation
content:
The months owed at the individual unemployability rate in the opening past-due release of a Disability Compensation award are:

| Individual unemployability on the decision history | Months owed at the individual unemployability rate |
|---|---|
| Granted with an effective date no later than the award's own | Every month owed |
| Granted with a later effective date | The whole months from its effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment |
| Not granted | None |

Those months take the individual unemployability rate of 3938.58 in place of the veteran-alone rate and their additions from the 100 percent tier — spouse 220.30, spouse aid and attendance 201.41, child 146.10, school child 472.95, parent 176.88 — and every other month owed takes its additions from the award's own tier. Individual unemployability's effective date is the effective date on the most recent rating decision granting it; the whole months counted from it are never fewer than nothing.

**Illustrations (hypothetical award effective 15 September 2025 at Disability Compensation (60% Combined Rating); most recent monthly payment issued 1 April 2026; 6 months owed)**

- Individual unemployability effective 15 September 2025 (the same day as the award): all 6 months at 3938.58.
- Individual unemployability effective 20 December 2025: whole months from 20 December 2025 to 1 April 2026 are 3; 3 months at 3938.58 and the other 3 at 1435.02, that is 11815.74 plus 4305.06, 16120.80 for the compensation owed.
- No individual unemployability on record: all 6 months at 1435.02.
